record.title: Entry record
record.description: One file per term, named for the term's slug. Every audience reads this file: the README, the site, and the issue form a contributor fills in.

issue.name: New entry
issue.description: Propose a term for the Civic Bestiary
issue.intro: Thanks for proposing a term. Pick the kind of thing you are naming first - a species is an actor you can point at, a move is an action you can watch, an ability is a capability an institution wields, a habitat is the place that houses them, a buff is a temporary condition, a fallacy is a documented argument, and a remedy or a keystone is a thing that answers one. Then fill in what you can; the maintainers handle placement, cross-references, and the final edit.
issue.identification_hint: Describe it the way its kind is described. Species: occasion, call, tell, counter. Move: trigger, tell, counter. Ability: effect, available to, counter. Habitat: carriers, economics, signature. Buff: effect, tell, expires. Fallacy: family, committed when, the tell, counter. Remedy: effect, costs, failure, tell. Keystone: office, call, tell, keystone.
issue.outro: A proposal lands as a record under `data/entries/<kind>/` once the writing holds up. The bar is not novelty, it is use: the term should name something a reader recognises and has no word for yet.

species.label: Species
species.blurb: A recognisable pattern of behaviour, worn like a costume - point at the pattern, not at a person.

identification.label: Occasion
identification.hint: The situation that calls it out: a decision that has to be defended, a correction that has to be answered, a ceremony that has to be filled. Structural, not demographic - name the moment, never the neighbourhood.
identification.example: A public decision that has to be defended by someone who did not make it.

identification.label: Call
identification.hint: The thing it says. A short quotation, ideally something you have actually heard.
identification.example: "Do you support the troops?"

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: How you recognise it before it speaks. Three is the house number.
identification.example: Flag decal on a leased vehicle

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: The thing that ends it, or makes it cost more than it returns.
identification.example: Answer the flag question, then ask the policy question again.

move.label: Move
move.blurb: An action performed in the open, in front of witnesses.

identification.label: Trigger
identification.hint: The moment it gets played - what has just happened that makes this the move to make.
identification.example: A question it cannot answer is on the floor.

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: What the move looks like from the gallery. The visible behaviour, not the motive.
identification.example: A request for definitions, repeated until the clock runs out.

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: The thing that ends it, or makes it cost more than it returns.
identification.example: Answer the question once, in writing, and move to close.

ability.label: Ability
ability.blurb: A capability an office, body, or machine can wield - no single person owns it.

identification.label: Effect
identification.hint: What it does to the board, in one sentence.
identification.example: Converts a map into a majority before a single vote is cast.

identification.label: Available to
identification.hint: Who can play it: an office, a chamber, a platform, a committee.
identification.example: State legislatures, once a decade, in a room with no cameras.

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: The rule, court, or practice that blunts it.
identification.example: An independent commission with a map-drawing mandate.

habitat.label: Habitat
habitat.blurb: The place a character is found and fed - the show, the rally, the forum - and the condition that would change what the room produces.

identification.label: Carriers
identification.hint: What carries it: channels, slots, rooms, platforms.
identification.example: Cable primetime, streaming specials, and the merch drop that follows.

identification.label: Economics
identification.hint: How the habitat pays for itself.
identification.example: Ad rates keyed to outrage, plus a subscription tier for the uncut version.

identification.label: Signature
identification.hint: The unmistakable formal tic - what makes it recognisably this habitat and not the news.
identification.example: A countdown clock over a battlefield.

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: What changes the room. Not a scolding - the condition, rule, or payment that would make this habitat a different place to stand in.
identification.example: A moderator with a published policy and a slow queue.

buff.label: Buff
buff.blurb: A temporary condition that changes what a character can get away with.

identification.label: Effect
identification.hint: What it changes about the bearer's behaviour or standing.
identification.example: Excuses any contradiction for the length of the news cycle.

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: How you spot someone carrying it.
identification.example: Confident mispronunciation of a thing they claim to have served in.

identification.label: Expires
identification.hint: What ends it, and roughly when.
identification.example: The first primary debate, or the first subpoena - whichever lands first.

fallacy.label: Fallacy
fallacy.blurb: A documented error in reasoning, named by logicians and psychologists - not a coinage, a real thing characters commit.

identification.label: Family
identification.hint: Where the accredited taxonomy files it: formal, or informal and which family.
identification.example: Informal · Relevance

identification.label: Committed when
identification.hint: The move that makes it happen, in plain terms.
identification.example: The claim is answered by attacking whoever made it.

identification.label: The tell
identification.hint: How you hear it in the room.
identification.example: The reply has no content about the claim, only about the claimant.

identification.label: Counter
identification.hint: The response that ends it.
identification.example: Ask what the claim gets wrong, and answer that instead.

remedy.label: Remedy
remedy.blurb: A procedure that works: what it does, what it costs the person using it, and how it gets captured.

identification.label: Effect
identification.hint: What it does to the character, in the active voice. One sentence, no moral.
identification.example: Turns a question into a deadline: the agency has to answer in writing, or say in writing why it will not.

identification.label: Costs
identification.hint: What it costs the person using it - time, money, exposure. A remedy with no price is a slogan.
identification.example: Fees, weeks, and the patience to appeal a redaction.

identification.label: Failure mode
identification.hint: How the remedy gets captured, defunded, or run out the clock. Every remedy has one, and naming it is the difference between a tool and a wish.
identification.example: The fee estimate that costs more than the record, and the exemption that arrives after the news cycle.

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: How you know it is working. Three is the house number.
identification.example: An answer with a docket number

keystone.label: Keystone
keystone.blurb: An office whose presence holds the ecosystem together - and whose absence is the whole problem.

identification.label: Office
identification.hint: What they hold, and what the rest of us borrow: the minutes, the roll, the record, the licence to ask.
identification.example: The minutes, the roll, and the file that proves both.

identification.label: Call
identification.hint: What they say, usually at the moment it is least convenient.
identification.example: "That's not in the record."

identification.label: Tell
identification.hint: How you know one when you meet one. Three is the house number.
identification.example: Reads the motion aloud, slowly

identification.label: Keystone
identification.hint: What collapses without them. Name the mechanism, not the moral - and name the character that needs the gap.
identification.example: Without the record there is no way to prove what the body did, which is the first thing a Sabotriot needs.

uses.label: Uses
uses.hint: The character or habitat wields this capability.

houses.label: Houses
houses.hint: The habitat is where this character, move, or fallacy is found. Author one direction; the other page says 'Found in'.

counters.label: Counters
counters.hint: The play that ends it, authored from the side that ends it. A remedy or a keystone may counter a character, a move, a power, a buff, or a habitat; the inverse page renders the other direction.

commits.label: Commits
commits.hint: The named fallacy this character's behaviour instantiates. This is the bridge between the guide's coinages and the documented taxonomy.

practises.label: Practises
practises.hint: The procedure this species actually runs, as opposed to the one it is accused of. Author the keystone, and the remedy's page lists who keeps it alive.

fields.label: Term
fields.hint: The coinage, spelled the way it should be listed. Title case, no quotes.
fields.example: <Term> - one word, title case, no quotes

fields.label: Kind
fields.hint: What sort of thing this is. A species is a person-shaped pattern, a move is an action, an ability belongs to an office, a habitat is a place that houses them, a buff is a condition, a fallacy is a documented error in reasoning, a remedy is a procedure that answers one, and a keystone is the office whose absence is the problem.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.hint: Which chapter the entry belongs to. The maintainers will move it if it belongs elsewhere.

fields.label: Position in chapter
fields.hint: Where the entry sits inside its chapter. Appending means one past the current highest.

fields.label: Sort scores
fields.hint: One score per axis the kind supports, 1-5. Impact is how much it does, abuse is how often it happens, blowback is what it costs the user.

fields.label: Part of speech
fields.hint: What the term is grammatically. Most species are nouns; moves are usually gerunds.

fields.label: Pronunciation
fields.hint: IPA between slashes. Approximate is fine.

fields.label: Etymology
fields.hint: Where the word came from, in one line. Name both parents if it is a blend.
fields.example: <parent> + <parent> - name both halves if it is a blend

fields.label: Senses
fields.hint: Two definitions: the thing itself, then the pattern it runs. Full sentences, one per line. The first sense becomes the page description, so make it stand alone.
fields.example: 1. <what it is, in one sentence> 2. <why it works, in one sentence>

fields.label: Example
fields.hint: One sentence in the wild, with the term in bold. Wrap the quotation in *asterisks*; the README renders it as an aside.
fields.example: *"<a line you could overhear>"* - the term in **bold**

fields.label: Easily confused with
fields.hint: Existing terms it could be mistaken for, and the one thing that tells them apart. Optional at proposal time - the maintainers add twins when the confusion is real.
fields.example: <Nearest neighbour> - the one thing that tells them apart

fields.label: Cross-references
fields.hint: Two or three existing terms this one belongs beside. The graph must stay connected, so every term needs at least one inbound reference.
fields.example: <Term>, <Term> - two or three that belong beside it

fields.label: Typed links
fields.hint: Relationship edges to other entries, each with a relation from the schema's vocabulary. Author one direction; the other page shows the inverse automatically.

fields.label: Source
fields.hint: Where the referent lives (label + URL), verified to resolve. A fallacy cites the documented account. A coinage cites the real institution, doctrine or procedure it is built on - Citizens United, the shadow docket, the pocket veto - because that is the thing a sceptical reader will look up. A character built on nothing real leaves this empty.

impact.label: Impact
impact.hint: How much damage it does to the thing it touches - public trust, a person's standing, the soundness of an argument.

abuse.label: Abuse
abuse.hint: How often you actually meet it. The axis that puts the popular ones first.

blowback.label: Blowback
blowback.hint: What it costs the one who uses it, once somebody notices.
